name: Lohara dynasty
alt: Kingdom of Kashmir under the Lohara dynasty

predecessors.name: Utpala dynasty
predecessors.text: Kashmir: Didda 'adopted as her heir' her nephew Samgrāmarāja, 'From this decision arose the Lohara dynasty of Kashmir'

successors.name: Kashmir Sultanate
successors.text: the Valley and its hills, taken by Shah Mir in 1339: 'he threw her and her children in prison while he himself ascended the throne as Sultan Shamsu'd-Din Shah'

ledger.x: 1003: Didda dies and her nephew Samgrāmarāja founds the Lohara dynasty of Kashmir.
1015: Mahmud of Ghazni besieges Lohkot.
1015: Mahmud abandons the siege and retreats to Ghazni, the result 'inconclusive'; he lost much of his army to attrition and winter.
1021: Mahmud returns to Lohkot.
1021: winter again defeats the Ghaznavids and Mahmud 'gave up on further plans of expansion into Kashmir'.
1056: Cliopatria's Kashmir shape loses its Jammu and Pir Panjal side.
1089: Utkarsa's accession reunites Kashmir with Lohara.
1101: Kashmir and Lohara part again.
1111: Sussala, who held Lohara, takes Kashmir.
1152: Cliopatria widens the Kashmir shape by about 199 cells (Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal).
1210: the Pothohar and Punjab foothills join Cliopatria's Kashmir shape.
1235: Kashmir becomes a Mongol dependency.
1320: Zulju's Mongols enter Kashmir.
1320: Zulju leaves with loot after widespread violence; the Valley is left to local chiefs and then Rinchan.
1320: the Mongol dependency is taken to end.
1320: Rinchan, a Ladakhi noble, takes the throne from the Lohara king Suhadeva (Zulju's raid had driven Suhadeva to Kishtwar).
1323: the Lohara line returns.
1338: the Shah Mir-Lohara war begins.
1339: Shah Mir wins.
1339: Lohara rule ends and the Shah Mir sultanate begins.

wars.name: Ghaznavid expeditions against Kashmir
wars.outcome: Both Ghaznavid sieges of Lohkot (1015, 1021) failed to the fortress and the winter; Kashmir kept its independence and Mahmud 'gave up on further plans of expansion into Kashmir'.

wars.name: Civil strife of Harsa, Uccala and Sussala
wars.outcome: Uccala and Sussala 'forced to flee in 1100'; Harsa murdered by the dāmaras in 1101; Kashmir and Lohara split under Uccala; Uccala's fall in December 1111 and Sussala's takeover of Kashmir.

wars.name: Zulju's raid on Kashmir
wars.outcome: The raid ends Suhadeva's rule: he flees to Kishtwar, the Valley passes to local chiefs, then Rinchan Shah.

wars.name: Shah Mir-Lohara war
wars.outcome: Shah Mir deposes Kota Rani and takes the throne in 1339, ending the Lohara line.

certainty.note: Mountain frontiers of a kingdom whose pages name only places (Srinagar, Loharkot, the Valley); nothing is sharp.
